candidates.title: The Availability & Supply of Critical Natural Resources for the Realization of a Fusion Pilot Plant: Fuels for Fusion (Pearson 2022, Kyoto Fusioneering / US DoE FES Workshop)
candidates.notes: Government workshop presentation (DOE FES, June 2022). Fully extracted via pdf_pipeline. Contains dedicated sections on beryllium supply chain including: resource base (100,000 tonnes USGS 2022), dominant supplier (Materion Corporation, Spor Mountain UT), current price ($610/kg beryllium alloy), toxicity/manufacturing challenges, one reactor requires approximately annual global supply of beryllium (Bradshaw et al. 2011), Materion S65 special grade with ultra-low uranium, export control issues, and fusion monopsony risk. Directly addresses G-10.

entries.notes: Pearson 2022 DOE presentation provides comprehensive beryllium supply chain data including current pricing ($610/kg), resource constraints (one pilot plant ≈ annual global supply), Materion monopoly, toxicity/manufacturing challenges, and fusion fleet scaling risks. candidates.title: Physics Basis of the Infinity Two Fusion Power Plant — JPP Collection
candidates.notes: Identified 6 papers in series (E65, E76, E83, E86, E88, E94). E86 (breeder blanket) mentions 'thermal efficiencies >30%' but no explicit value. No paper in the collection covers balance-of-plant or power conversion efficiency specifically.

candidates.title: Overview of the Helios Design: A Practical Planar Coil Stellarator Fusion Power Plant (Thea Energy)
candidates.notes: Direct stellarator BOP analog. Confirms: 40% Rankine thermal efficiency, 1.1 GW thermal from 958 MW fusion (blanket multiplier ~1.15), 438 MWe gross, 390 MWe net, steam superheated to 635°C. Low recirculating power consistent with steady-state stellarator advantage. Freely accessible on arXiv.

entries.notes: No Infinity Two–specific thermal efficiency value published. Provides independent constraint on the 38–42% implied range in the analysis. Gap remains partial — Infinity Two thermal efficiency is still derivable, not directly published.
